classification.difficultyReason: Construct a limiting tangent and resolve a two-stage golf trajectory into perpendicular components.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
This diagram represents a golfer at $G$, 80 m from the centre of a green, $C$, which can be represented by a circle of diameter 12 metres.

Calculate, to two decimal places, the greatest angle that the golfer can deviate either side of the direct line $GC$ so that the golfer’s ball can land on the green.

spec.description: Schematic unshaded green and centre-distance dimension. Ordinary source blue lines and red point markers use house black.
spec.mathematics: GC=80 m; circle diameter 12 m; no tangent or deviation angle supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: No solution construction or answer is visible.

answer.short:
$4.30^\circ$ either side of $GC$.

The limiting line is tangent to the green.
answer.worked:
Let $H$ be a point of tangency from $G$, and let $\theta=\angle CGH$. A radius is perpendicular to the tangent, so $\angle GHC=90^\circ$ and $CH=6$ m.

$$\begin{align*}\sin\theta&=\frac{6}{80}\\\theta&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{6}{80}\right)\\\theta&\approx4.30^\circ.\end{align*}$$

Thus the greatest deviation is $4.30^\circ$ either side of $GC$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: This diagram below represents a 350 m golf hole. $TD$ and $DF$ represent the centre line of the fairway, with $\angle TDF=120^\circ$, $TD=200$ m and $DF=150$ m. The golfer hits 220 m, $10^\circ$ left of the line $TD$, to a point, $X$. Find the distance, correct to two decimal places, from $X$ to $F$.

spec.description: Coordinate-derived golf-hole geometry retaining the horizontal TD, rising TX and falling DF. Ordinary source colours use house black.
spec.mathematics: TD=200 m, DF=150 m, TX=220 m, angle XTD=10 degrees and angle TDF=120 degrees. XF is not supplied.

answer.short:
$177.94\text{ m}$.

Resolve the paths horizontally and vertically, then use Pythagoras’ theorem.
answer.worked:
Take $TD$ as horizontal. Since $180^\circ-120^\circ=60^\circ$, the horizontal and downward components of $DF$ are $150\cos60^\circ=75$ m and $150\sin60^\circ=75\sqrt3$ m.

Relative to $T$, $F$ is $275$ m horizontally to the right and $75\sqrt3$ m below. The corresponding components of $TX$ are $220\cos10^\circ$ m right and $220\sin10^\circ$ m up.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Horizontal separation}&=275-220\cos10^\circ\\\text{Vertical separation}&=220\sin10^\circ+75\sqrt3\\XF^2&=(275-220\cos10^\circ)^2+(220\sin10^\circ+75\sqrt3)^2\\XF&=\sqrt{(275-220\cos10^\circ)^2+(220\sin10^\circ+75\sqrt3)^2}\\XF&\approx177.94\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
